newsitem.title: USA: Foreign share of Japan's chip market rises.
newsitem.headline: Foreign share of Japan's chip market rises.

text.p: The Japanese market share of international computer chipmakers selling products was a near-record 29.4 percent in the fourth quarter, reflecting a push by U.S. and European companies, the U.S. Semiconductor Industry Association said Thursday.

The fourth-quarter figures for 1996 fell short of the record set in the fourth quarter of 1995, when foreign chip companies had 29.6 percent of the market, the industry group said. But results for the most recent fourth quarter were more than 2 percentage points higher than the third quarter.
U.S., European and Korean chip companies have been clamoring for a bigger share of the Japanese chip market, the second biggest after the United States.

Semiconductor trade has been a touchy issue between Washington and Tokyo since the mid-1980s. Through two official trade agreements and recent industry summits, foreign chip companies have increased their share.
Daryl Hatano, acting president of the Semiconductor Trade Association, said in a statement that with U.S. expertise in chip design and manufacturing, "we should expect increased share."
Earlier this month, American, Japanese, European and Korean chip executives met in Hawaii for an industry summit to find ways to lower restrictions on international trade in semiconductors.
